concepts.title: Cartesian Product of Sets
concepts.definition: The cartesian product of sets A and B is the set of all ordered pairs with first element from A and second from B, written A cross B, and the number of ordered pairs equals the product of the sizes of the two sets.
concepts.key_idea: If A has m elements and B has n elements, A cross B has m times n ordered pairs, and two ordered pairs are equal when corresponding elements are equal.

concepts.title: Relations: Domain, Range and Number of Relations
concepts.definition: A relation R from A to B is a subset of the cartesian product A cross B, its domain is the set of first elements and range the set of second elements, and the total number of relations from A to B equals two raised to the product of the numbers of elements.
concepts.textbook_ref: Every subset of A cross B defines a relation, so a small set pair can carry many relations.

concepts.title: Functions: Definition, Domain, Range and Types
concepts.definition: A function from set X to set Y assigns to every element of X exactly one element of Y, with domain, codomain and range, and special types include identity, constant, polynomial, rational and modulus functions shown by graphs.
concepts.key_idea: Every function is a relation but not every relation is a function, since the exactly one condition fails for arbitrary relations.
